en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 14.1.
Hetuduka (The Dyad on Causes)
Hetu:
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent on a state that is a cause (hetu), a state that is not a cause arises by way of the cause-condition (hetupaccaya)—dependent on a state that is a cause, the associated states...
The aggregates and mind-produced matter; at the moment of rebirth-linking ... [etc.
... dependent on a root phenomenon, a non-root phenomenon arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a root phenomenon, both root and non-root phenomena arise by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause (na-hetu), a state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya).

Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, a state that is a root-cause arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is not a root-cause, states that are both root-causes and not root-causes arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root-cause and not a root-cause, a state that is not a root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root-cause and not a root-cause, a state that is not a non-root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both a root-cause and not a root-cause, states that are both not a root-cause and not a non-root-cause arise by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-condition (hetu), there are nine; in the case of object-condition (ārammaṇa), nine ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance-condition (avigata), nine. (The sections on co-nascence, association, and so forth are similar to the section on dependence.
Root-Object: A state that is a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is not a root ... three.
A state that is a root-cause (hetu) is a condition, by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya), for a state that is not a root-cause; [three].
A state that is not a root-cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not a non-root-cause; [three].
States that are both root-causes and not root-causes are conditions, by way of object-condition, for a state that is not a root-cause; [three]. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root-cause condition, three; in object condition, nine ... pe ... in decisive support condition, nine; in prenascence and postnascence conditions, three; in repetition condition, nine;
in kamma condition, three; in resultant condition, nine; in nutriment condition, three; in faculty condition, nine; in jhāna condition, three; in path condition, nine;
in association condition, nine; in dissociation condition, five ... pe ... in non-disappearance condition, nine. (The "Questions" section should also be expanded in this manner.)
